bounded_statement: For the selected result only: the two-sample pooled-variance Student t test reported as t = 5.200, df = 46, p < 0.0001 entered all 48 nightly recording sessions as independent observations, although the data description declares bat_id as the independent unit and each of the 12 bats contributes 4 repeated nights. Within-bat night-to-night variation (~0.15-0.2 kHz SD) is far smaller than between-bat variation (~1.8 kHz SD), so rows are strongly clustered by bat. A bat-level reanalysis (one mean per bat, 6 vs 6) yields the same 2.600 kHz mean difference but t ≈ 2.43 on df = 10, p ≈ 0.035; the reported df and p-value overstate the evidence, though the direction and nominal significance at α = 0.05 survive aggregation.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses its unit choice, stating that the 12 bats each contributed 4 sessions and that individual sessions were the units entered into the test; one could argue the session-level analysis was intentional. However, disclosure does not make repeated sessions from the same bat independent under the declared unit (bat_id), so this does not rescue the reported df or p-value.

counterevidence_considered.description: The qualitative conclusion is not reversed by correct unit handling: aggregating to one mean per bat preserves the 2.600 kHz mean difference (quarry_adit higher) and remains nominally significant (t ≈ 2.43, df = 10, p ≈ 0.035). This bounds severity to overstated precision/df rather than a wrong-direction or sign-flipped conclusion.

evidence.description: The input data contain four rows per bat; e.g. bat QA01 contributes four nightly rows with nearly identical peak frequencies (38.4-38.8 kHz), illustrating strong within-bat clustering relative to the ~1.7 kHz between-bat spread.
The analysis code appends every row's frequency to its site's sample and feeds those row-level samples directly into a pooled two-sample t test, with no per-bat aggregation anywhere in the workflow.
The report's selected result claims t = 5.200 on df = 46 with p < 0.0001, explicitly stating that all 48 nightly sessions were entered as 48 observations.

source_refs.quoted_text:

- Two-sided p-value: p < 0.0001

[selected-result] Two-sample t test over 48 nightly recording sessions entered as 48 observations: mean peak echolocation frequency is 2.600 kHz higher at quarry_adit than at halden_culvert (t = 5.200, df = 46, p < 0.0001).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the issue two ways. (1) Checked whether rows might be effectively independent despite sharing bat_id: computed within-bat SDs from the CSV (~0.15-0.2 kHz, e.g. QA01: 38.5/38.8/38.4/38.7) versus between-bat SD of per-bat means (~1.85 kHz per site); clustering is strong, so row independence fails empirically as well as by declaration. (2) Checked whether the reported numbers could instead reflect a bat-level analysis: recomputed per-bat means (quarry_adit: 38.6, 39.5, 40.3, 41.7, 42.5, 43.4; halden_culvert: 41.8, 39.3, 37.6, 37.5, 37.1, 37.1), giving pooled SD 1.849, SE 1.068, t ≈ 2.43, df = 10, p ≈ 0.035 — which does not match the reported t = 5.200, df = 46; the reported values instead exactly match the 48-row calculation (pooled SD 1.732, SE 0.500, t = 2.600/0.500 = 5.200, df = 24+24-2 = 46). Both falsification routes failed, confirming the row-level entry of repeated per-bat measurements.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py builds the two test samples by appending every CSV row's peak_frequency_khz to its roost site's list (freq[site].append(khz)) and passes those row-level lists directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind(left, right, equal_var=True), with no per-bat aggregation, clustering adjustment, or mixed model. The four repeated nights from each marked bat are therefore treated as four independent observations in a procedure whose validity assumes row independence, inflating the effective sample size from 12 bats to 48 sessions and the degrees of freedom from 10 to 46.
